'''Robert Barry Hobson Coates''' (born 18 October 1956) is a New Zealand politician who was a member of the [[New Zealand House of Representatives]] as a representative of the [[Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand]]. Since 2019<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=About us |url=https://mindfulmoney.nz/about/about-us/ |access-date=2024-03-22 |website=mindfulmoney.nz |language=en}}</ref> he has been chief executive of the [[ethical investment]] charity Mindful Money.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Our People - Barry Coates |url=https://mindfulmoney.nz/people/details/barry-coates/ |access-date=2024-03-22 |website=mindfulmoney.nz |language=en}}</ref>

==Environmental career==
Coates worked for the [[government of Samoa]] from 1978 to 1980, promoting the development of small business.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.oxfam.org.nz/about-us/who-we-are/barry-coates |title=Barry Coates |date=7 March 2014 |publisher=[[Oxfam]] | accessdate=5 September 2016}}</ref> He has a bachelor of Commerce from the [[University of Auckland]] and a Masters in Public and Private Management from the [[Yale School of Management]].<ref name="auto">{{cite news |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/element-magazine/news/article.cfm?c_id=1503340&objectid=11166339 |title=Oxfam Executive Director turns to politics |first=Sophie |last=Barclay |date=3 December 2013 | work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] | accessdate=5 September 2016}}</ref>

Coates worked at World Wide Fund for Nature [[WWF-UK]] from 1991, until 1996. He was an NGO observer on the British government delegation to the [[Earth Summit]] (the United Nations Conference on Environment and Development) at [[Rio de Janeiro]] in 1992, and was closely involved in sustainable development policy in the UK and internationally.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Anderson |first1=Megan |title=Barry Coates – Pacific watchdog on the world |url=http://pacific.scoop.co.nz/2009/10/barry-coates-pacific-watchdog-on-the-world/ |publisher=Pacific Scoop |accessdate=5 September 2016 |date=19 October 2009}}</ref>

He was Executive Director of the World Development Movement (subsequently renamed [[Global Justice Now]]) from 1996 until 2003. During this time he played a leading role in international research and campaigns on trade and investment agreements, sustainable development, corporate accountability, Third World debt and international aid and development policy.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://home.greens.org.nz/candidates/barry-coates |title=Barry Coates |publisher=[[Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand]] |accessdate=5 September 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160827133056/https://home.greens.org.nz/candidates/barry-coates |archive-date=27 August 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Coates was the Executive Director of [[Oxfam]] New Zealand from September 2003,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.oxfam.org.nz/about-us/who-we-are/barry-coates|title=Barry Coates|date=2014-03-07|work=Oxfam NZ|access-date=2017-04-05|language=en}}</ref> and he stepped down on 7 March 2014 to contest the [[2014 New Zealand general election|general election]] for the [[Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand|Green Party]] in the [[Mount Roskill (New Zealand electorate)|Mount Roskill electorate]].<ref name="auto"/> He subsequently developed a programme on sustainability for the [[University of Auckland Business School]], and was Coordinator of "It's Our Future", the campaign against the Trans-Pacific Partnership Agreement (TPPA).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.greens.org.nz/candidates/barry-coates-mp|title=Barry Coates MP|website=Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand|language=en|access-date=2017-04-05|archive-date=2 May 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170502195604/https://www.greens.org.nz/candidates/barry-coates-mp|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 5 September 2016, it was announced that [[Kevin Hague]] intended to resign from the House of Representatives, and that Coates would replace him as a list MP.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/83930082/greens-leadership-kevin-hague-hopeful-quits |title=Green MP quits | work=[[Stuff.co.nz]] | date=5 September 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11704046|title=Kevin Hague quits Greens for Forest and Bird|date=5 September 2016|website=[[The New Zealand Herald]]|accessdate=5 September 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA1611/S00327/barry-coates-celebrates-sustainability-champion-award.htm|title=Barry Coates named Sustainability Champion winner at 2016 NZI Sustainable Business Network Awards|date=18 November 2016|via=Scoop Independent News}}</ref>

On 7 October 2016, he was officially sworn in as Member of the House of Representatives and member of the Green Party parliamentary caucus.

Coates suggested in a July 2017 post on the left-wing "The Daily Blog" that the Green Party might force a second election if the [[New Zealand Labour Party|Labour Party]] formed a coalition with [[New Zealand First]] without the Greens.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Coates|first1=Barry|title=Great Together|url=https://thedailyblog.co.nz/2017/07/11/great-together/|website=The Daily Blog|accessdate=11 October 2017}}</ref> His comments were challenged by co-leader [[James Shaw (New Zealand politician)|James Shaw]] who stated that forcing a hung parliament or second election was "absolutely not" the party's position.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11889937|title=Green MP's comments on NZ First the 'height of stupidity' - Winston Peters|author=Davison, Isaac|date=13 July 2017|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]}}</ref> As number 10 on the party's list, he was not re-elected when the Greens elected only 8 MPs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elections.org.nz/events/2017-general-election/2017-general-election-party-lists|title=2017 General Election Party Lists|website=Elections.org.nz|accessdate=30 September 2018}}</ref>

==Post-politics==
Following the 2017 general election, Coates founded the consumer awareness organisation "Mindful Money", which focuses on ethical investment practices.<ref name="North & South March 2024">{{cite journal |last1=MacDonald |first1=Theo |title=How much a dollar cost? |journal=[[North & South (New Zealand magazine)|North & South]] |date=March 2024 |pages=42–45 |url=https://northandsouth.co.nz/2024/02/19/israel-war-affects-your-kiwisaver/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240418234111/https://northandsouth.co.nz/2024/02/19/israel-war-affects-your-kiwisaver/|archive-date=18 April 2024|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In October 2019, Coates praised the Sustainable Finance Forum's draft report advocating ethical investment particularly the transition towards a low-emissions economy and inclusiveness.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Coates |first1=Barry |title=Barry Coates: Why green is good for business |url=https://northandsouth.co.nz/2024/02/19/israel-war-affects-your-kiwisaver/ |access-date=18 April 2024 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=31 October 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240418234640/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/business/barry-coates-why-green-is-good-for-business/XSHQZK5QNYP3JCQGOHJUL67U2Q/|archive-date=18 April 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2019, Mindful Money convinced several fund managers at [[KiwiSaver]] to reconsider their investments in nuclear weapons manufacturing. As a result, investment in nuclear weapons dropped from $100 million in 2019 to below $10 million in 2024. Following the [[Gaza war]], Coates and [[Francesca Albanese]] (the [[United Nations Special Rapporteur on the occupied Palestinian territories]]) met with 10 KiwiSaver managers to petition them to divest from companies identified by Mindful Money or the [[United Nations Human Rights Council]] as support [[Israeli settlements]] in the West Bank. Mindful Money was criticised by Dr David Cumin of the pro-Israel lobby group "Israel Institute of New Zealand" for an alleged "undue fixation" on Israel. Coates disagreed with Cumin's assertion, saying that Mindful Matters was focusing on companies violating ethical standards and international humanitarian and human rights laws.<ref name="North & South March 2024" />
